paragraphs.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are of the Dispersion, greeting.
paragraphs.original: Ἰάκωβος θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ χαίρειν.
paragraphs.translit: Iakōbos theou kai kyriou Iēsou Christou doulos tais dōdeka phylais tais en tē diaspora chairein.

paragraphs.text: Count it all joy, my brethren, when ye fall into manifold temptations;
paragraphs.original: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε, ἀδελφοί μου, ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις,
paragraphs.translit: Pasan charan hēgēsasthe, adelphoi mou, hotan peirasmois peripesēte poikilois,

paragraphs.text: Knowing that the proving of your faith worketh patience.
paragraphs.original: γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν·
paragraphs.translit: ginōskontes hoti to dokimion hymōn tēs pisteōs katergazetai hypomonēn·

paragraphs.text: And let patience have [its] perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, lacking in nothing.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω, ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι, ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι.
paragraphs.translit: hē de hypomonē ergon teleion echetō, hina ēte teleioi kai holoklēroi, en mēdeni leipomenoi.

paragraphs.text: But if any of you lacketh wisdom, let him ask of God, who giveth to all liberally and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
paragraphs.original: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας, αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος, καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: Ei de tis hymōn leipetai sophias, aiteitō para tou didontos theou pasin haplōs kai mē oneidizontos, kai dothēsetai autō·

paragraphs.text: But let him ask in faith, nothing doubting: for he that doubteth is like the surge of the sea driven by the wind and tossed.
paragraphs.original: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ·
paragraphs.translit: aiteitō de en pistei, mēden diakrinomenos, ho gar diakrinomenos eoiken klydōni thalassēs anemizomenō kai rhipizomenō·

paragraphs.text: For let not that man think that he shall receive anything of the Lord;
paragraphs.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου
paragraphs.translit: mē gar oiesthō ho anthrōpos ekeinos hoti lēmpsetai ti para tou kyriou

paragraphs.text: a doubleminded man, unstable in all his ways.
paragraphs.original: ἀνὴρ δίψυχος, ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: anēr dipsychos, akatastatos en pasais tais hodois autou.

paragraphs.text: But let the brother of low degree glory in his high estate:
paragraphs.original: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Kauchasthō de ho adelphos ho tapeinos en tō hypsei autou,

paragraphs.text: and the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de plousios en tē tapeinōsei autou, hoti hōs anthos chortou pareleusetai.

paragraphs.text: For the sun ariseth with the scorching wind, and withereth the grass: and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his goings.
paragraphs.original: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον, καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο· οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: aneteilen gar ho hēlios syn tō kausōni kai exēranen ton chorton, kai to anthos autou exepesen kai hē euprepeia tou prosōpou autou apōleto· houtōs kai ho plousios en tais poreiais autou maranthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been approved, he shall receive the crown of life, which [the Lord] promised to them that love him.
paragraphs.original: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν, ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς, ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Makarios anēr hos hypomenei peirasmon, hoti dokimos genomenos lēmpsetai ton stephanon tēs zōēs, hon epēngeilato tois agapōsin auton.

paragraphs.text: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God; for God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempteth no man:
paragraphs.original: μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ θεοῦ πειράζομαι· ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν, πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα.
paragraphs.translit: mēdeis peirazomenos legetō hoti Apo theou peirazomai· ho gar theos apeirastos estin kakōn, peirazei de autos oudena.

paragraphs.text: but each man is tempted, when he is drawn away by his own lust, and enticed.
paragraphs.original: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος·
paragraphs.translit: hekastos de peirazetai hypo tēs idias epithymias exelkomenos kai deleazomenos·

paragraphs.text: Then the lust, when it hath conceived, beareth sin: and the sin, when it is fullgrown, bringeth forth death.
paragraphs.original: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν, ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον.
paragraphs.translit: eita hē epithymia syllabousa tiktei hamartian, hē de hamartia apotelestheisa apokyei thanaton.

paragraphs.text: Be not deceived, my beloved brethren.
paragraphs.original: μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.
paragraphs.translit: mē planasthe, adelphoi mou agapētoi.

paragraphs.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation, neither shadow that is cast by turning.
paragraphs.original: Πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν, καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν φώτων, παρʼ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα.
paragraphs.translit: Pasa dosis agathē kai pan dōrēma teleion anōthen estin, katabainon apo tou patros tōn phōtōn, parʼ hō ouk eni parallagē ē tropēs aposkiasma.

paragraphs.text: Of his own will he brought us forth by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
paragraphs.original: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας, εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων.
paragraphs.translit: boulētheis apekyēsen hēmas logō alētheias, eis to einai hēmas aparchēn tina tōn autou ktismatōn.

paragraphs.text: Ye know [this], my beloved brethren. But let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
paragraphs.original: Ἴστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι, βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν,
paragraphs.translit: Iste, adelphoi mou agapētoi. estō de pas anthrōpos tachys eis to akousai, bradys eis to lalēsai, bradys eis orgēn,

paragraphs.text: for the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.
paragraphs.original: ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην θεοῦ οὐκ ἐργάζεται.
paragraphs.translit: orgē gar andros dikaiosynēn theou ouk ergazetai.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
paragraphs.original: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: dio apothemenoi pasan rhyparian kai perisseian kakias en prautēti dexasthe ton emphyton logon ton dynamenon sōsai tas psychas hymōn.

paragraphs.text: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deluding your own selves.
paragraphs.original: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Ginesthe de poiētai logou kai mē akroatai monon paralogizomenoi heautous.

paragraphs.text: For if any one is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a mirror:
paragraphs.original: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής, οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ,
paragraphs.translit: hoti ei tis akroatēs logou estin kai ou poiētēs, houtos eoiken andri katanoounti to prosōpon tēs geneseōs autou en esoptrō,

paragraphs.text: for he beholdeth himself, and goeth away, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.
paragraphs.original: κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν.
paragraphs.translit: katenoēsen gar heauton kai apelēlythen kai eutheōs epelatheto hopoios ēn.

paragraphs.text: But he that looketh into the perfect law, the [law] of liberty, and [so] continueth, being not a hearer that forgetteth but a doer that worketh, this man shall be blessed in his doing.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας, οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου, οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de parakypsas eis nomon teleion ton tēs eleutherias kai parameinas, ouk akroatēs epilēsmonēs genomenos alla poiētēs ergou, houtos makarios en tē poiēsei autou estai.

paragraphs.text: If any man thinketh himself to be religious, while he bridleth not his tongue but deceiveth his heart, this man`s religion is vain.
paragraphs.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία.
paragraphs.translit: Ei tis dokei thrēskos einai mē chalinagōgōn glōssan autou alla apatōn kardian autou, toutou mataios hē thrēskeia.

paragraphs.text: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this, to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, [and] to keep oneself unspotted from the world.
paragraphs.original: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν, ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν, ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου.
paragraphs.translit: thrēskeia kathara kai amiantos para tō theō kai patri hautē estin, episkeptesthai orphanous kai chēras en tē thlipsei autōn, aspilon heauton tērein apo tou kosmou.
